documents.unit: Library and ITS / Teaching & Learning Commons
documents.title: Library and ITS Guidance for Faculty on Artificial Intelligence
documents.summary: Guidance to faculty from Academic Technology and the Libraries: put an AI statement in the syllabus and in assignments, redesign assignments, mind privacy and copyright, and do not rely on detectors. No required rule.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no college rule on student AI use. It "recommend[s] providing clear guidance on acceptable use of AI in your class" and says some assignments may use AI while others may not, leaving the decision to each instructor.

units.why: The page tells faculty that "Critical evaluation of any AI platform you consider integrating ... is key", a recommendation to instructors to vet AI tools before adopting; P65 (review of tools) is nearest although this is an individual duty, not an institutional review.
units.anchor: Critical evaluation of any AI platform you consider integrating into your teaching
units.fit_note: Frames tool evaluation as an individual faculty duty rather than an institutional review or approval step.

units.why: "will often 'hallucinate' and create convincing-looking but fake citations" is a statement of fact about output reliability, so P31 (AI output is often wrong) with informs modality.
units.anchor: will often "hallucinate" and create convincing-looking but fake citations or untrue statements

units.why: The page lists "serious concerns about bias in the training sets ... unfair labor practices ... and the environmental impact", naming harms; P53 matches exactly.
units.anchor: serious concerns about bias in the training sets the AI models use, unfair labor practices

units.why: "You should also consider issues of copyright and fair use when designing an assignment" tells instructors to weigh copyright, which is P52.
units.anchor: You should also consider issues of copyright and fair use when designing an assignment

units.why: "Academic Technology and Swarthmore Libraries are constantly vetting generative AI tools" describes an institutional vetting activity, which is P65 (review of tools); it is informational, not a rule.
units.anchor: are constantly vetting generative AI tools

units.why: "Swarthmore has options for tools that we license which can provide more control" points to institution-wide licensed tools, so P92 rather than the course-specific P17.
units.anchor: Swarthmore has options for tools that we license which can provide more control

units.why: "We can help you and your students make an informed decision" offers staff support for faculty deciding on AI tools; P63 (support faculty in learning AI) fits.
units.anchor: We can help you and your students make an informed decision

units.why: "We recommend providing clear guidance on acceptable use of AI in your class" asks instructors to put AI expectations in the course; P09 (AI statement in syllabus) is the best fit even though the modality is a recommendation.
units.anchor: We recommend providing clear guidance on acceptable use of AI in your class

units.why: The guidance says to use "a general statement on your syllabus and/or course site, as well as specific policies for individual assignments", leaving the rule to instructor and assignment: P04 (per instructor or assignment) not P09, since the point is the two-level setting.
units.anchor: specific policies for individual assignments
units.frag_start: This might include a general statement

units.why: The page offers "Three policy examples from Harvard" ranging from "maximally restrictive (no AI use)" to "fully-encouraging" and "mixed", presenting a spectrum of levels as models; P05 (named tiers) fits partly because the page only points to examples.
units.anchor: a maximally restrictive policy (no AI use), a fully-encouraging policy, and a mixed use policy
units.fit_note: Points to external sample policies at three levels; Swarthmore itself defines no tiers.

units.why: "We also recommend providing guidance on the transparent use of AI tools, such as writing a statement of use" asks instructors to have students disclose AI use, which is P24.
units.anchor: writing a “statement of use” as part of an assignment
units.fit_note: Addressed to instructors as advice on what to require; options are a statement of use or a bibliography citation.

units.why: "Most disciplinary professional organizations now provide clear citation guidelines and templates, such as the MLA, APA, and Chicago" tells how to cite AI, a factual pointer; P25 (cite tool, prompt, output) is nearest.
units.anchor: Most disciplinary professional organizations now provide clear citation guidelines and templates
units.fit_note: Points to external style guides; does not itself require tool, prompt or date.

units.why: "In some cases you may want to thoughtfully experiment with the use of AI tools ... but there may be other assignments that you prefer students complete without" leaves AI permission to each assignment: P04.
units.anchor: there may be other assignments that you prefer students complete without the aid

units.why: "ITS and the Libraries can assist you in the creation of dynamic new assignments or the redesign of existing activities" is staff support for instructors redesigning assignments; P63 (support faculty) over P35 because it offers help, not a redesign rule.
units.anchor: ITS and the Libraries can assist you in the creation of dynamic new assignments

units.why: "Requiring a personal reflection or connection to current events" is suggested to ensure students create their own work, an assignment redesign: P35.
units.anchor: Requiring a personal reflection or connection to current events

units.why: "Including an oral component or presentation" is listed as a way to ensure students create their own work, so understanding is checked by explaining: P34.
units.anchor: Including an oral component or presentation

units.why: "Documenting the process with rough drafts and revisions" asks students to keep drafts that track progress: P26 (keep drafts) rather than P40 because the drafts are submitted by students as evidence of their own work.
units.anchor: Documenting the process with rough drafts and revisions
units.fit_note: Process documentation proposed as assignment design, not a disclosure of AI use.

units.why: "Have students use generative AI and critique the output" proposes building AI use into an assignment, which is P79 (require AI use in some coursework).
units.anchor: Have students use generative AI and critique the output

units.why: "Instead of summarizing a reading, try using social annotation tools such as Perusall" suggests replacing a summary assignment with a tool that resists AI shortcuts: P35.
units.anchor: Instead of summarizing a reading, try using social annotation tools
units.frag_end: support in using these easy-to-learn tools)

units.why: "Instead of writing a long-format analysis, try a multimodal project" is another assignment redesign suggestion: P35.
units.anchor: Instead of writing a long-format analysis, try a multimodal project

units.why: "you can schedule a conversation with an Academic Technologist and/or a librarian to help you design, implement, and assess these assignments" offers staff help to instructors: P63.
units.anchor: schedule a conversation with an Academic Technologist and/or a librarian

units.why: "Most free AI tools ingest user data for training purposes. Submitting student work ... has privacy risks" states a data-privacy fact, so P50 informs.
units.anchor: Most free AI tools ingest user data for training purposes

units.why: "We do not recommend entering or uploading any intellectual property, including your own scholarship, research data, student work" advises faculty against uploading to free tools; P50 (protect data) because the stated reason is data and legal risk, and P49 is about students uploading course materials.
units.anchor: We do not recommend entering or uploading any intellectual property

units.why: "uploading copyrighted or licensed content may violate legal agreements" warns of a legal consequence of uploading, P52 (licensing, copyright).
units.anchor: uploading copyrighted or licensed content may violate legal agreements

units.why: "Swarthmore has licensed platforms through which we can mitigate risks and adjust settings" recommends licensed tools as the safer path: P92.
units.anchor: Swarthmore has licensed platforms through which we can mitigate risks

units.why: "discuss your ideas with a Librarian or Academic Technologist to evaluate potential use cases" asks instructors planning an AI-based assignment to consult staff before use, closest to P63 (support for faculty) with an element of review.
units.anchor: discuss your ideas with a Librarian or Academic Technologist
units.fit_note: Also a consult-before-adopting step that works like informal tool review.

units.why: "We don't believe that there is a tool available that can definitively detect AI use" says detectors are unreliable: P39.
units.anchor: We don't believe that there is a tool available that can definitively detect AI use

units.why: "We discourage efforts to submit all student work to a system to attempt to determine if AI was used" tells instructors not to run blanket detection, P39 (do not rely on detectors).
units.anchor: We discourage efforts to submit all student work to a system

units.why: "the TLC sponsors regular discussions on the subject as part of their Inquiry Group series" offers a faculty community on generative AI: P63.
units.anchor: the TLC sponsors regular discussions on the subject as part of their Inquiry Group series

documents.unit: Library and ITS / Teaching & Learning Commons
documents.title: Library and ITS Guidance For Students On Artificial Intelligence
documents.summary: Student-facing checklist on genAI covering policy checks, citation, privacy, tool choice, ethics, environmental impact and prompting. Defers course-level rules to professors.
documents.stance_why: The page tells students to "clarify each professor's genAI policies before using any genAI tools" and says rules differ by course. It sets only one firm ban (uploading course materials without permission) and otherwise gives advice, so the decision sits with instructors.

units.why: The page defines "generative AI" as "tools that use generative models based on deep learning to create predictive text, images, or code" and names examples, setting the scope: P61.
units.anchor: generative models based on deep learning to create predictive text, images, or code

units.why: "In some cases, it might be difficult to determine if you are using 'artificial intelligence' or not" says the boundary of AI is fuzzy, part of defining scope: P61.
units.anchor: it might be difficult to determine if you are using
units.fit_note: Admits the scope is hard to determine rather than defining it.

units.why: "Academic Technology and Swarthmore Libraries can help you make an informed decision about when, how, and which generative AI tools" directs students to human help: P72.
units.anchor: can help you make an informed decision about when, how, and which generative AI

units.why: "Swarthmore has options for tools that we license which can provide more control" refers to institution-wide licensed tools: P92.
units.anchor: Swarthmore has options for tools that we license which can provide more control

units.why: "Do not enter or upload any course materials ... to a genAI tool without permission" is a direct prohibition on students uploading course materials: P49.
units.anchor: Do not enter or upload any course materials

units.why: "Each professor may have different rules about genAI use in their courses or for specific assignments" says rules differ by instructor: P04 (instructor sets rule) rather than P11 since the point is who decides.
units.anchor: Each professor may have different rules about genAI use in their courses

units.why: "Always clarify each professor's genAI policies before using any genAI tools" makes students responsible for finding out each course's rules: P78.
units.anchor: Always clarify each professor’s genAI policies before using any genAI tools

units.why: "Make sure that using genAI tools align with your professor's guidelines as well as the College's academic misconduct policy" ties AI use to existing rules: P77.
units.anchor: align with your professor’s guidelines as well as the College’s
units.fit_note: Does not state AI misuse is misconduct; only says use must align with the misconduct policy.

units.why: "Consider if genAI tools are enhancing your understanding or simply completing tasks for you" asks students to keep their own learning central: P32.
units.anchor: Consider if genAI tools are enhancing your understanding or simply completing tasks

units.why: "if the goal of the assignment is for you to think critically about a text or to develop your writing or coding skills, then using AI to do that work for you would not be appropriate" bars outsourcing work to AI when it defeats the learning goal: P19.
units.anchor: using AI to do that work for you would not be appropriate
units.fit_note: Conditional on the assignment goal; also explains the skill-building reason (P41).

units.why: "Using genAI inappropriately can hinder your educational experience" gives the learning reason for limits: P41.
units.anchor: Using genAI inappropriately can hinder your educational experience

units.why: "Output from genAI tools isn't necessarily factually accurate" warns of errors: P31.
units.anchor: Output from genAI tools isn’t necessarily factually accurate

units.why: "it's important to verify those sources and the claims being made" tells students to verify AI citations and claims: P31 must-style duty.
units.anchor: it’s important to verify those sources and the claims being made

units.why: "We recommend you always cite the use of a genAI tool just as you would any research source or scientific instrument" asks for citing AI use, P24; the source analogy is secondary.
units.anchor: always cite the use of a genAI tool just as you would any research source
units.fit_note: Also treats AI like a research source or instrument (P45/P96 territory).

units.why: "Which tool you used, how you used it, and why you used it will matter" names the details a citation includes (tool, how, why): P25.
units.anchor: Which tool you used, how you used it, and why you used it will matter

units.why: "We recommend writing a statement of use as part of an assignment and/or citing the integration of AI generated materials as part of a bibliography" gives the two forms disclosure takes: P24.
units.anchor: writing a “statement of use” as part of an assignment and/or citing

units.why: "You should cite any text, images, media, or data analysis you have generated with AI tools" sets what must be cited: P24.
units.anchor: You should cite any text, images, media, or data analysis you have generated

units.why: "Avoid entering personal, sensitive, or identifiable information into genAI platforms" is a data-protection rule: P50.
units.anchor: Avoid entering personal, sensitive, or identifiable information into genAI platforms

units.why: "Always read and understand privacy agreements to make informed decisions about the information you share" tells students to read platform privacy terms: P50.
units.anchor: Always read and understand privacy agreements

units.why: "companies may have policies regarding genAI use during the application and interview process. Confirm what's acceptable" addresses AI in job applications, a rule outside coursework that fits no type.
units.anchor: Confirm what's acceptable before using genAI tools for resumes, cover letters, and interviewing
units.uncovered_note: Students should check employers' rules before using genAI for job or internship applications.

units.why: "email career@swarthmore.edu to explore genAI tools to assist you with interviewing, resume writing" points students to Career Services, a human office that helps with AI: P72.
units.anchor: explore genAI tools to assist you with interviewing, resume writing, and job market

units.why: "Who owns, sponsors, or controls this site? Make sure the company is transparent about the terms and conditions" asks students to vet a tool's provider and terms: P50 (vetted tools) with partial fit.
units.anchor: Make sure the company is transparent about the terms and conditions
units.fit_note: Asks students to judge a provider's transparency, not to use a vetted list.

units.why: "Is the tool compatible with your needs? Was it designed for the purpose or goal" asks students to match tool to task, which no type covers.
units.anchor: Was it designed for the purpose or goal you are trying to achieve
units.uncovered_note: Students should choose a genAI tool designed for the task they have (code, data, images, video).

units.why: "did you consult with an expert on campus who can provide you with access to our licensed software" directs students to staff and licensed tools: P92.
units.anchor: an expert on campus who can provide you with access to our licensed software
units.fit_note: Also directs students to human experts (P72).

units.why: "Are the ethical implications worth the use of these platforms for your purposes?" asks students to weigh risks and benefits including bias, labor exploitation and copyright: P53.
units.anchor: Have you weighed the benefits and risks of using genAI platforms?

units.why: "Are you offloading critical thinking in a problematic way by using this tool?" asks students to keep their own thinking: P32.
units.anchor: Are you offloading critical thinking in a problematic way by using this tool?

units.why: The section "Environmental Impacts of AI" asks about "water consumption" and strain on "the electric grid", naming environmental costs: P53.
units.anchor: Why does AI require increased

units.why: The page lists "College Supported GenAI Tools" (Librechat, Google Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Adobe Firefly), naming institution-approved tools: P92.
units.anchor: College Supported GenAI Tools

units.why: The prompt tips ("Define your audience ... tone ... scope ... output") are practical advice on prompting: P93.
units.anchor: providing detailed and specific prompts is key to getting the best possible result

units.why: "Provide references - but only materials that you have permission to share with the model" repeats the permission limit on uploads inside prompt advice: P49.
units.anchor: but only materials that you have permission to share with the model

units.why: "Always evaluate your results critically, and check your sources" tells students to scrutinize AI output: P31.
units.anchor: Always evaluate your results critically, and check your sources.

documents.title: Guidelines on the Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)
documents.summary: ITS guidelines for the college community: protect non-public data, get ITS approval before buying AI tools, verify AI output, optionally cite it, and expect change. Coursework use is left to departments and instructors.
documents.stance_why: The guidelines say "individual departments are encouraged to discuss and develop their own internal approach" and do not address coursework use. They restrict only sensitive data and tool purchasing, so they set no stance on AI in learning.

units.why: "generative AI has the potential to enhance how education is delivered ... customized learning plans, brainstorm alongside researchers, reduce the time spent on administrative tasks" names benefits: P87.
units.anchor: generative artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to enhance how education is delivered

units.why: "necessitates a set of guidelines that ensure accountability, transparency, and academic integrity" states the purpose of the guidelines: P56.
units.anchor: necessitates a set of guidelines that ensure accountability, transparency, and academic integrity

units.why: "use of AI should follow the applicable policies and standards" in IT policies, the Student Code of Conduct and the Employee handbook is a compliance rule: P77.
units.anchor: use of AI should follow the applicable policies and standards outlined

units.why: "individual departments are encouraged to discuss and develop their own internal approach to using AI" lets departments set their own rules: P85.
units.anchor: individual departments are encouraged to discuss and develop their own internal approach

units.why: "Community members should keep the following guidelines in mind when using AI technologies" sets the scope as the whole community: P56.
units.anchor: Community members should keep the following guidelines in mind when using AI technologies

units.why: "the sharing of any non-public, confidential, proprietary, or otherwise sensitive information to any AI tool is not permitted" without a protective contract is a firm data rule: P50.
units.anchor: any non-public, confidential, proprietary, or otherwise sensitive information to any AI tool is not permitted

units.why: "Swarthmore College does not have a specific contract or agreement with most AI tools" is the fact that makes the data rule bite: P50 informs.
units.anchor: does not have a specific contract or agreement with most AI tools or services

units.why: "Swarthmore's Purchasing Policy requires ITS approval for purchasing software application contracts" applies to AI tools: P65.
units.anchor: requires ITS approval for purchasing

units.why: "Before procuring AI tools, submit a support ticket to the ITS Service Portal" with the data classification: a procedural step in tool approval, P65.
units.anchor: Before procuring AI tools, submit a support ticket to the ITS Service Portal
units.frag_end: will be used with the tool.

units.why: "ITS will review the tool, evaluating based on security, data management, cost, accuracy/reliability, accessibility, bias/ethical concerns" lists review criteria: P65.
units.anchor: ITS will review the tool, evaluating based on security, data management
units.frag_end: potential alternative tools to accomplish the need.

units.why: "You are responsible for verifying the accuracy of content created with the assistance of AI" is a duty to verify: P31, with accountability for content.
units.anchor: You are responsible for verifying the accuracy of content created with the assistance of AI

units.why: "Content generated with the assistance of AI should always be manually checked for accuracy and bias" extends the check to bias: P31.
units.anchor: should always be manually checked for accuracy and bias

units.why: "Those choosing to make use of AI tools should familiarize themselves with the policies and practices of the specific platform" is advice to know platform terms: P50.
units.anchor: should familiarize themselves with the policies and practices of the specific platform being used
units.fit_note: About platform policies generally, not only privacy.

units.why: "consider including citation, attribution, and/or an explanation of how the tool was used" when sharing AI-assisted material is soft disclosure: P24.
units.anchor: consider including citation, attribution, and/or an explanation of how the tool was used
units.fit_note: Hedged by Where appropriate and consider.

units.why: "these guidelines are subject to change" says the guidance is provisional: P54.
units.anchor: As AI technology is rapidly evolving, these guidelines are subject to change

units.why: "They are not intended to replace existing College policy" says the guidelines sit under existing policy: P77.
units.anchor: They are not intended to replace existing College policy

units.why: "If you have specific questions regarding the use of AI at Swarthmore College, please contact support@swarthmore.edu" names the contact for questions: P80, partial fit since it names a help desk not an owner.
units.anchor: please contact support@swarthmore.edu for additional guidance
units.frag_start: If you have specific questions regarding
units.fit_note: Names a help channel for questions rather than an office that interprets or enforces the policy.

notes: No school or computing-unit policy found; course layer deferred. Two UNCOVERED units both in the student guidance (employer rules for job applications; choosing a tool fit for the task). ITS page also links an 'AI Guidelines for Staff' page that was not in the collected set.
